body:
Thanks for reporting this @PCRedHot. I suspect this is related to integer overflow.

In the example code above, it looks like `data_array_cupyx` is cast from `uint8` to `int8` via `astype`, but this wasn't done in the SciPy case? The range of uint8 is [0, 255] but int8 is [-128, 127] so this is not a safe type conversion and may overflow (e.g. try `np.arange(256).astype(np.int8)` and you will see all values >=128 have wrapped around to negative values).

If that is not the source of the difference, please try two other things to help us debug:
1.) If you change CuPy to use `output=cp.float64` and don't cast to an integer type, how similar are the values to SciPy with dtype=np.float64? It should be extremely close (to within some floating point rounding error)
2.) For the same `output=cp.float64` in CuPy, what is `data_array_cupyx.max()`? 

The interpolation itself is always done in a floating point precision internally and ultimately cast back to the requested output dtype, so it is possible there is some difference in behavior of that conversion that we did not test for, but I am not sure yet without more info.

@grlee77 Thanks for replying. Actually I was casting to ```uint8``` not ```int8```, sorry for the typo.

### Changing to ```float64```
For faster computation, I use one of the slice of the array instead of the full 4d array.
```python3
import numpy as np
import cupy as cp
import cupyx.scipy.ndimage
import scipy.ndimage

# Inputs:
# orginal_array: 3d uint8 numpy shape: (208, 208, 224) 
# space_directions: [0.97212501, 1.37501857, 1.15326139]

data_array_cupyx = cupyx.scipy.ndimage.zoom(cp.array(original_array, dtype=cp.uint8), space_directions, output=cp.float64).get()
data_array_scipy = scipy.ndimage.zoom(np.array(original_array, dtype=np.uint8), space_directions, output=np.float64)

print(data_array_cupyx.max())
# >>> 277.9522959942204

# Differences
diff_array = data_array_cupyx != data_array_scipy
abs_diff_array = np.abs(data_array_scipy[diff_array] - data_array_cupyx[diff_array])
print('Different Values:', np.sum(diff_array), 'out of', np.prod(data_array_cupyx.shape))
# >>> Different Values: 14831388 out of 14905176
print('Mean:', np.mean(abs_diff_array))
# >>> Mean: 9.753422964007812e-07
print('Max Diff:', np.max(abs_diff_array))
# >>> Max Diff: 4.2252419405031105e-05
print('Min Diff:', np.min(abs_diff_array))
# >>> Min Diff: 3.6403788870864156e-109
```
If I change the array to ```float64``` first:
```python3
import numpy as np
import cupy as cp
import cupyx.scipy.ndimage
import scipy.ndimage

# Inputs:
# orginal_array: 3d uint8 numpy shape: (208, 208, 224) 
# space_directions: [0.97212501, 1.37501857, 1.15326139]

data_array_cupyx = cupyx.scipy.ndimage.zoom(cp.array(original_array, dtype=cp.float64), space_directions, output=cp.float64).get()
data_array_scipy = scipy.ndimage.zoom(np.array(original_array, dtype=np.float64), space_directions, output=np.float64)

print(data_array_cupyx.max())
# >>> 277.95229920482706

# Differences
diff_array = data_array_cupyx != data_array_scipy
abs_diff_array = np.abs(data_array_scipy[diff_array] - data_array_cupyx[diff_array])
print('Different Values:', np.sum(diff_array), 'out of', np.prod(data_array_cupyx.shape))
# >>> Different Values: 12155420 out of 14905176
print('Mean:', np.mean(abs_diff_array))
# >>> Mean: 4.030957640523563e-15
print('Max Diff:', np.max(abs_diff_array))
# >>> Max Diff: 1.9895196601282805e-13
print('Min Diff:', np.min(abs_diff_array))
# >>> Min Diff: 3.9815085624544553e-119
```

Yes, I think making the output to be ```float64``` would slove the problem.
```python3
import numpy as np
import cupy as cp
import cupyx.scipy.ndimage
import scipy.ndimage

# Inputs:
# orginal_array: 3d uint8 numpy shape: (208, 208, 224) 
# space_directions: [0.97212501, 1.37501857, 1.15326139]

data_array_cupyx = cupyx.scipy.ndimage.zoom(cp.array(original_array, dtype=cp.float64), space_directions, output=cp.float64).get().astype(np.uint8)
data_array_scipy = scipy.ndimage.zoom(np.array(original_array, dtype=np.float64), space_directions, output=np.float64).astype(np.uint8)

print(data_array_cupyx.max())
# >>> 277.95229920482706

# Differences
diff_array = data_array_cupyx != data_array_scipy
abs_diff_array = np.abs(data_array_scipy[diff_array] - data_array_cupyx[diff_array])
print('Different Values:', np.sum(diff_array), 'out of', np.prod(data_array_cupyx.shape))
# >>> Different Values: 0 out of 14905176
```

Perhaps outputing directly as ```uint8``` will trigger this problem.
I tested the whole 4d data with input ```float64```, output ```float64``` and then ```astype(np.uint8)```. It does not appear to have any difference now. Thank you for helping. :)

Okay, that is good that the floating point case followed by casting is consistent. That shouldn't be necessary as ideally `output=cp.uint8` should work the same way as in scipy. If you are able to make a small subset of the data where you see the issue available for us to test with, that could help look into it a bit more.

Sure, here is a subset of the data. [part.zip](https://github.com/cupy/cupy/files/8220508/part.zip)

### Script
```python3
import numpy as np
import cupy as cp
import cupyx.scipy.ndimage
import scipy.ndimage

numpy_file_path = 'path_to/part.npy'

space_directions = [0.97212501, 1.37501857, 1.15326139]
original_array = np.load(numpy_file_path)

# original_array shape: (208, 208, 224) uint8

data_array_cupyx = cupyx.scipy.ndimage.zoom(cp.array(original_array, dtype=cp.uint8), space_directions, output=cp.uint8).get()
data_array_scipy = scipy.ndimage.zoom(np.array(original_array, dtype=np.uint8), space_directions, output=np.uint8)

# new array shape: (202, 286, 258)

# Differences
diff_array = data_array_cupyx != data_array_scipy
print('Different Values:', np.sum(diff_array), 'out of', np.prod(data_array_cupyx.shape))
# >>> Different Values: 568 out of 14905176
```
